subject: itemfit sensitive regarding number of respondents?

messages.author: ed2ac94694ffb33f
messages.subject: itemfit sensitive regarding number of respondents?
parts:
Dear mirt-group

 

I´ve a question regarding case size sensitivity of itemfit statistics.

I tried to fit the same model (likert scale „graded response“) to two different data sets which are quite comparable.

Most parameters are quite similar, but the itemfit (in this case S_X2) is fine for the smaller one (about 1000 respondents) but not for the bigger one (about 25000 respondents).

 

Is this normal and does anyone have an idea or is the solution as simple as using e.g. 'X2*_df' or 'X2*'?

 

Thank you very much in advance and especially Phil for your package

 

Best

 

Janine

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: itemfit sensitive regarding number of respondents?
parts:
Hi Janine,

Yes, this is normal and expected behaviour with goodness-of-fit statistics. The bases for these and other measures is to test for *exact* fit, which in reality is extremely unlikely to be strictly true, so increasing sample size may trivially trigger significance tests even though the discrepancy is minor. Looking at ratios such as χ2 / df​​ may be helpful, though these are really just rules of thumb. Also, inspecting the pattern of the residuals will be helpful here too (statistics like S-X2 can compute tables, and there are some other two-step graphical procedures that mirt supports which may provide reasonable approximations of the functional forms). HTH.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: itemfit sensitive regarding number of respondents?
parts:
itemfit() has an argument S_X2.tables = TRUE, which will generate the table of expected/observed counts given the conditional total scores. See also the itemGAM function for a visual analogue with a general purpose smoother (similar approach to using the empirical.plot input within itemfit(), though doesn't rely on "binning" ranges to construct counts). HTH.

Phil
